note: Block Permissions owns no configuration object at all - its entire surface is dynamic permissions generated by BlockPermissionsPermissions::permissions() via permission_callbacks, plus _custom_access requirements bolted onto six core block routes by its RouteSubscriber. So every medium/hard case is grounded in real user.role.* config and the exact permission strings 'administer block settings for theme <theme>' and 'administer blocks provided by <provider>'. The themes used (olivero, claro) are the two installed, non-hidden themes on this site, which are exactly the ones the callback emits permissions for. The missing-theme introspection case exercises the module's documented gotcha: 'administer blocks' plus a provider permission is still a 403 on /admin/structure/block without the default theme's permission.

evals.prompt: The Drupal contrib module block_permissions adds finer-grained block permissions. What are the two families of permission names it generates, and how are they generated?
evals.expected_output: They are generated dynamically: block_permissions.permissions.yml contains only a permission_callbacks entry pointing at BlockPermissionsPermissions::permissions(). That emits 'administer block settings for theme <theme_machine_name>' for every installed non-hidden theme, and 'administer blocks provided by <provider>' for every distinct provider in the block plugin definitions.

evals.prompt: A Drupal role has the core 'administer blocks' permission but still gets access denied on /admin/structure/block after the block_permissions module was enabled. What is missing?
evals.expected_output: The route block.admin_display gets an extra _custom_access requirement, BlockPermissionsAccessControlHandler::blockListAccess, which checks 'administer block settings for theme ' . config('system.theme')->get('default'). So the role also needs the permission for the site's default theme, e.g. 'administer block settings for theme olivero'.

evals.prompt: Which core block routes does the Drupal block_permissions module alter, and what does it change on each of them?
evals.expected_output: Its RouteSubscriber adds _custom_access requirements to block.admin_display (blockListAccess), block.admin_display_theme and block.admin_library (blockThemeListAccess), block.admin_add (blockAddFormAccess - needs both provider and theme permission), and entity.block.edit_form / entity.block.delete_form (blockFormAccess - provider permission). block.admin_library additionally gets its controller replaced with BlockPermissionsBlockLibraryController::listBlocks, which filters out blocks the user cannot add.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a role with the machine name bp_known_role that was set up using the block_permissions module. Inspect the live site and tell me which theme's block layout that role may administer, and which block provider's blocks it is allowed to manage.
evals.expected_output: Theme claro and provider views: user.role.bp_known_role holds 'administer blocks', 'administer block settings for theme claro' and 'administer blocks provided by views'. `drush cget user.role.bp_known_role permissions` shows all three.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the role bp_locked_role has the 'administer blocks' permission, but users in it still get access denied on /admin/structure/block. Inspect the live site (its permissions and the site's theme settings) and tell me exactly which permission has to be added to fix it.
must_contain_any: administer block settings for theme olivero
evals.expected_output: 'administer block settings for theme olivero'. system.theme:default is olivero, and block_permissions adds a _custom_access check (blockListAccess) to block.admin_display that requires 'administer block settings for theme ' . the default theme. bp_locked_role only has 'administer blocks' and 'administer blocks provided by system'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a user role with the machine name bp_task_role, labelled 'BP task role'. Using the block_permissions module, give it the ability to manage the block layout of the Olivero theme and to manage blocks provided by the block_content module, and nothing more (it must not be able to administer blocks on the Claro theme). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Role bp_task_role holds 'administer block settings for theme olivero' and 'administer blocks provided by block_content' (plus core's 'administer blocks'), and does NOT hold 'administer block settings for theme claro'.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a role called 'BP claro role' (machine name bp_claro_role). People in it should be able to move blocks around on the administration pages - the Claro theme - but only the blocks that come from Drupal's user module, and they must not be able to touch the blocks on our public Olivero theme. Set that up on the live site.
evals.expected_output: bp_claro_role gains 'administer block settings for theme claro' and 'administer blocks provided by user', with no other 'administer blocks provided by ...' permission and without 'administer block settings for theme olivero'.
